lore:
He saw the church spire melting like a candle, its waxen remains dripping onto the priest's pure-white wings.
The saints depicted in the stained-glass windows rapidly rotted into skeletons, then instantly regressed into infants.
Sharp and soft geometric shapes spilled from the mouths of the faithful, filling the entire hall.

He saw the train station fold repeatedly into non-Euclidean space. The distant platform was almost within reach, while the nearby ticket gate lay impossibly far away.
The clock in the hall turned counterclockwise. The bony crowd walked backward, pulled along by invisible strings, as thick violet smoke drifted from the clouds into the mouth of the train.

He saw the "void" in the forest take shape. Trees, rocks, and vines merely traced the translucent outline drawn by the void.
The swan's feathers shifted constantly through mosaic colors, and wherever it swam, the lake water hardened into translucent stained glass.
Beneath the bench where couples cuddled, a vivid orange-yellow shadow gnawed at its owner's ankle.

He saw the notes of the opera hall rain down upon the audience. He saw the graveyard gently rise and fall, like the skin of a breathing giant.

He saw so much—far too much.

He told his mother, his teachers, and his friends what he saw, and painted those visions into his artwork. He wanted to place the world he had witnessed before the eyes of others.
But the people around him gradually grew fewer, while one world drifted farther and farther away from him.

Why was this happening?
He was merely recording what he saw.
Pickman could not understand.

A sorrowful Pickman stood before the mirror.
In its reflection, he saw a ghoul grinning at him with sharp, bloodstained teeth.

"There is nothing more important than witnessing reality. Madness, chaos, greed...
"Do you want to see, Pickman?"

The enlightened Pickman smiled at him and stepped into the mirror.
He had only wanted to witness reality's most extreme madness with his own eyes and faithfully depict it on canvas.

He was neither human nor ghoul.
He was simply Pickman, the realist painter.
